complete: He grumbled, then he lit them. That's the whole of soldiering.
Take the shield. It has the castle's mark, and the watch will know you by it.

done: The road is lit, the bridge is held, and the market comes in the morning. That's a castle.

princes_hunt.name: The Prince's Hunt

talk: My father says a prince does not go wolf hunting. My father says a great many things.
There is a den of timber wolves north of Ashvale - real wolves, not Whisperwood's greys. Four of them. Then tell me how it went, in detail.
progress: The Timber Wolf Den is north of Ashvale, past the dragon road. Bring a bigger weapon than you think.
complete: Four! And you came back with all your fingers. I am going to tell everyone it was my idea.

talk: Two pelts, for a cloak. If I cannot hunt, I can at least look as though I did.
The tailor in Ashvale can sew it, if Mother asks her. Mother will ask; she likes a story as much as I do.
progress: Two timber wolf pelts. The greys' pelts are too thin; a prince has standards.
complete: Look at that. Nobody will believe a word of it, and that is the best part.

done: The cloak is finished. He wears it to dinner. The king pretends not to notice.

realm_accounts.name: Accounts of the Realm

talk: A castle runs on bread, iron and accounts, and I am short of accounts.
Odric the merchant passes through Ashvale. Ask him what goods move on the road and what they fetch. Write nothing down; merchants lie less to people who are not writing.
progress: Odric trades in Ashvale. He will have a wagon, or a story about where it went.
complete: Salt, hides and gossip, and the gossip sells best. Noted.

talk: Now Hollis at the Saltmere tap. Every price in the valley is argued about in a tavern before it is agreed anywhere else.
Ask him what a barrel of salt fish fetches this month, and what it fetched last. The difference is the news.
progress: Hollis keeps the Tap in Saltmere. Buy something; it loosens the numbers.
complete: Excellent. Now I know what everything costs, and I can complain about it properly.

done: The ledgers balance, for once. He has asked to be left alone with them.

lodge_gifts.name: Gifts for the Lodges

talk: The king sends seals. I prefer to send someone who will sit down and ask what is wanted.
Go to the lodges by Ziibiing and ask Mishoomis what a gift from the castle ought to be. Then come back and tell me before the king guesses.
progress: The lodges are beside Ziibiing. Mishoomis is the one people go to first.
complete: Hides, he said, good ones, for the winter. Sensible. The king would have sent silver spoons.

talk: Three deer hides, then. The deer keep to the open woods; a bow helps, patience helps more.
Bring them to me, not the king. He will want to add a letter, and the letter will be about himself.
progress: Three deer hides. Not goat, not boar - the lodges will know the difference, and so will I.
complete: These will go west with the next drover. A gift that is wanted is worth ten that are admired.

done: The hides went west. A letter came back, and the king was not allowed to read it first.

even_ground_visit.name: The Even Ground

talk: Every map in the keep has a blank where the Even Ground should be. Somebody drew it once and somebody else scraped it off.
Go and see it for me. There is someone there called Vael. Ask what the blank is for.
progress: The Even Ground is east of Ashvale, through the woods. Mind where you step; the maps did.
complete: Vael said it is kept blank on purpose. That is the most interesting thing anyone has said to me all year.

talk: One more blank: the dragon road. The squire who keeps it writes to nobody, which is suspicious in a squire.
Go and say the castle asks after him. Then come and tell me everything he did not say.
progress: Squire Elian keeps the dragon road, north of the village. He will be standing as though he is guarding something.
complete: He asked for nothing and said less. I shall draw him on the map as a very small question mark.

done: Two blanks fewer. She has started a new map, and it has room at the edges.

kings_seal.name: The King's Seal

talk: The castellan tells me the road is lit and the bridge is held. Then it is time the castle had friends at the end of it.
Take my seal to Mayor Calder in Saltmere. A castle with a harbour for a friend is a castle with a future.
progress: Mayor Calder keeps the town hall in Saltmere, past the docks.
complete: He took the seal and kept it. That is as good as a yes from a mayor.

talk: Now the people of Ziibiing, on the river far to the west. They were here before the castle and they will be here after it.
Go to Nookomis. Do not take the seal - take my word, and listen to hers.
progress: Ziibiing is a long road. Nookomis will be by the fire, or the river, or wherever she likes.
complete: She said we may visit, if we come to learn. I think that is the best treaty I will ever sign.

done: The seal is in Saltmere and my word is in Ziibiing. The valley is larger than it was this morning.

beyond_the_mountain.name: Beyond the Mountain

talk: You came over the mountain? Then you're the first person I've seen in a fortnight who isn't a goat.
There's country beyond here nobody at the castle has walked. Smoke, some evenings, to the west. Tell Orla at the lodge what I've seen; she keeps the trail log.
progress: Orla's lodge is at the castle side of the mountain, at the foot of the safe road. Tell her about the smoke.
complete: She wrote it down? Then it's real now. That's how trails work.

talk: Now the castellan. If there's a town out west, the castle will want to know before it wants anything from us.
Tell him the trail's open both ways. Tell him I said the smoke smells of bread, which is either good news or a very clever trap.
progress: Castellan Brannoc is in the Lake Castle's inner ward, by the keep door.
complete: He's sending word west. Whatever's out there, you'll be the one who gets to find it.

done: The trail log has a new page headed 'West', and nothing written under it yet.

the_high_pass.name: The High Pass

talk: That's the dangerous climb behind me. I tell everyone to take the safe road, and everyone thinks I'm being polite.
There's a band of cutthroats camped on the high pass, in the snow, taking a toll from anyone fool enough to go up. Four of them, if you're the fool.
progress: The pass is at the top of the climb, where the snow starts. Bring a warm cloak and a sharp sword, in that order.
complete: Four. The toll's lifted, then. I'll pretend I didn't hope you'd come back.

talk: The bandits were the polite ones. Frost goblins have moved into the rocks above the pass, and they don't take tolls.
Three of them, and the climb's as safe as a climb like that ever gets.
progress: The goblins keep to the rocks above the pass. They're small, they're cold, and they're quicker than they look.
complete: Three. I'll still tell folk to take the safe road. But now I'll mean it a little less.

done: Bryn has started letting people up the climb. He still glares at them.

flask_for_the_hermit.name: A Flask for the Hermit

talk: There's an old man on the west ledge, up the safe road, who will not come down and will not starve either, if I can help it.
Take him this flask of broth while it's hot. Stay on the road; the mountain is generous with ways to fall off it.
Then come back and tell me he drank it, not that he said he would.
progress: Aled's ledge is up the safe road, past the shrine, round the west shoulder. Bring me back his thanks.
complete: He drank it? All of it? Then he'll live till spring out of sheer stubbornness.
That's one errand off my list and three more on it. Welcome to the lodge.

done: The broth goes up every week now. Aled says it is too salty, which means he likes it.

wolves_on_the_climb.name: Wolves on the Climb

talk: Crag wolves have come down the east face, bolder than they ought to be, and they've had two of my snares and one of my dogs.
The warden keeps folk off that climb for good reason. You're not folk, apparently. Four of them, on the crags.
progress: The crags are up the dangerous climb from Warden Bryn's post. They hunt in pairs; don't let them pick the ground.
complete: Four. The dogs will sleep tonight and so will I.

talk: Now the pelts, two of them. A winter on this mountain is a long thing to do without fur.
Wolf from the crags or from the den north of Ashvale, I'm not fussy. The cold isn't either.
progress: Two timber wolf pelts. The crag wolves drop them, and so do the ones north of the village.
complete: Good thick ones. I'll have a coat by the first snow and a story to tell about it.

done: The lodge has a new rug and fewer visitors with teeth.

echo_riddle.name: The Echo's Question

talk: The echoes up here have been asking me a riddle for thirty years, and I am tired of being the only one who answers.
I sleep in a pocket and wake with a scrape. I hold a fire I never feel. Bring me one of me.
One, mind. The echoes count, and they are pettier than I am.
progress: Sleeps in a pocket, wakes with a scrape, holds a fire it never feels. Any shop in the valley sells the answer.
complete: A tinderbox. The echoes say it was too easy. The echoes always say that.

talk: Now a harder one, and not for you. Go to Wyn at the shrine and ask him what the stones were before they were stones.
He's been not telling me for twenty years. Perhaps he'll not tell you instead, and then come back and say what he didn't say.
progress: Wyn's shrine is down the road, on the north shoulder. Ask him. Then come back up and tell me.
complete: Mountains, he said? Before they were stones they were mountains. Insufferable. And true, which is worse.

done: The echoes have a new riddle now. Aled will not tell anyone what it is, which he enjoys enormously.

three_stones.name: The Three Stones

talk: The stones do not speak to the impatient, so sit, or stand still at least, which is nearly the same.
Bring them three gifts: one that kept a beast warm, one that once stood taller than you, and one that is all that remains.
Lay them before me together. The stones dislike being visited in instalments.
progress: What kept a beast warm, what once stood tall, what remains. All three at once. Tobin's sheep below the castle wear the first.
complete: The sheep's coat, the fallen tree, the last of a life. Yes. Listen - the stones are pleased, in their slow way.

talk: A second riddle, since the first did not frighten you. Bring me two that are weak apart and strong together.
Smiths know them. Soldiers owe their lives to them. Neither one would say thank you to the other.
progress: Two that are weak apart and strong together. Ask a smith, if you must. Smiths love to be asked.
complete: Copper and tin, and between them, bronze. You think in metals now. The mountain approves of that.

done: The stones hum when you pass. Wyn says it is gratitude; the hermit says it is wind.

scattered_tomes.name: The Scattered Tomes

talk: The Circle once had three books worth keeping. In a weak moment, years apart, I lent all three to people who live on this mountain.
Aled on the ledge has the Tome of Echoes, Wyn at the shrine the Tome of Stones, and Tamsin at the Far Foot the Tome of the Far Road.
Start with Aled. He will say he has not finished it. He has had it for thirty years.
progress: Aled's ledge is down the safe road's west shoulder. Ask him for the Tome of Echoes.
complete: The Tome of Echoes? Take it. I know it by heart, and the echoes know it better. Tell Halvard I found the ending sad.

talk: Wyn has the Tome of Stones. Wyn will want to tell you what it means, at length, beside the stones.
Let him. It is cheaper than arguing, and he is usually right.
progress: The shrine is on the north shoulder, on the safe road. Ask Wyn for the Tome of Stones.
complete: The book of the stones. Read the third chapter by them sometime; they like to hear it. Go carefully, it is older than the shrine.

talk: The last is the Tome of the Far Road, with Tamsin at the Far Foot. She borrowed it for the maps and kept it for the warnings.
It is the one I most want back. Do not read the last page on the way up. Or do, and then walk faster.
progress: Tamsin waits at the Far Foot, at the bottom of both ways on the far side. Ask her for the Tome of the Far Road.
complete: The Far Road? Here. I copied the maps. I didn't copy the last page; I didn't want it in my own hand.

talk: All three. Read them on the way up, if you have not; they were written to be read side by side, and they sulk apart.
Then show them to Pell. He keeps the Circle's catalogue, and he has been waiting thirty years to tick them off.
progress: Show the three tomes to Pell at his stall in the yard. Keep them after; the Circle lends its books to its friends.
complete: Echoes, Stones, the Far Road - all three ticked! The Archmage read the last page over your shoulder. He says the chain hums colder than last year.
Keep them. He says a book on a shelf up here helps nobody, and you have already read the part that matters.

done: The three books sit side by side in the tower now. Halvard reads the last page of the third one every night.

archmage_trial.name: The Archmage's Trial

talk: The Circle takes no members who cannot keep a road. Watching the stars is easy; getting home from watching them is not.
Clear the pass of three bandits. Then three frost goblins. Then come back up and we will see about a cloak worthy of the name.
progress: Three pass bandits on the High Pass, then three frost goblins.
complete: Three bandits. Now the goblins, and then come up.

talk: The goblins now. Three. They will be expecting you, having heard the bandits.
Come back up when it is done. The cold will tell me before you do.
progress: Three frost goblins in the rocks above the pass.
complete: The road is kept. Take this focus: ice from the summit that has not melted since the chain was forged.
Welcome to the Circle of the Long Night. Pell will sell you the cloak at a member's price, which is the same price, said more warmly.

done: You are of the Circle now. Halvard nods when you pass, which from him is a speech.

stolen_ink.name: The Stolen Ink

talk: The Circle writes in frost ink. It does not fade, it does not run, and the frost goblins think it is the shiniest thing in the world.
They have stolen a winter's worth from our stores and taken it down to the rocks above the pass.
Persuade three of them that ink is not worth it. I leave the method to you, but I am a wizard, and I have an opinion.
progress: The frost goblins keep to the rocks above the High Pass. Three of them.
complete: Three. They will tell the others, in their fashion, which is mostly shrieking.

talk: Now the ink itself. Three pots. The goblins carry it about with them because they cannot think where else to put it.
If a pot is cracked, bring it anyway. Frost ink in a cracked pot is still frost ink, only colder.
progress: Three pots of frost ink. The frost goblins above the pass carry it.
complete: Three, and not one opened. You have more patience than any apprentice I have ever had.

done: Pell has labelled the ink cupboard 'NOT FOR GOBLINS'. The Archmage says this will not help.

tower_beacon.name: The Frostspire Beacon

talk: You climbed up here on purpose? Then you can be useful on purpose. The beacon at the top of the tower has gone out.
It is not a pretty light. It tells the valley the Circle is still watching, and it tells the things in the dark the same.
Five logs. There are no trees up here, which is why nobody up here has any.
progress: Five logs for the beacon. The pines on the way up the safe road will give them, if you bring a hatchet.
complete: Five. Dry, too. It will be lit within the hour, and the castle will see it from the walls.

talk: Now tell Pell the beacon is fed. He keeps the log of it, and he will want to write something important-sounding in it.
Do not let him sell you anything while you are there. Or do. I am not your mother.
progress: Pell is at his stall in the yard. Tell him the beacon is fed.
complete: Beacon fed! I'll write it down. 'Fed, by a traveller, with logs.' The Archmage says my entries are too long.

done: The beacon burns every night now. The Archmage pretends not to look at it from the yard.

hollow_den.name: The Hollow Den

talk: Come in out of the wind, traveller. I am Isolde, and these walls of stakes are all that is left to the Thornwatch.
We kept the abbey on the ridge for three hundred years. Then something woke beneath it, and our own sisters turned their bows on us. We ran. Sisters do not run.
There is a cave on the Red Moor, past the old foundations, with skulls cut into the rocks at its mouth. The Hollow Den.
Whatever is calling the dead up out of the moor, it is gathering there. I can feel it when I close my eyes, like heat from a banked fire.
Go down and clear it. All of it, every last creature, or it will only fill again. Do that, and the Sisters will remember your name.
progress: {left} still stir in the den, {name}. I can feel them. Search every chamber; they like the dead ends.
The little red ones run when their pack breaks. Let them go and they come back with friends. Kill the firecaller first.
Elin sells my potions by the gate. Take more than you think you need.
complete: It's quiet. I felt it the moment the last of them fell: like a window opening in a stuffy room.
Cinderhide. So that was the heat. We buried him on the moor two winters ago; he didn't stay buried.
Take this shield with the Sisters' thanks; it hung in the abbey's chapel. And this stone: hold it and think of our fire, and the ring by the back wall will bring you home.
You fight like one of us. That is the highest praise I have.

done: The moor feels lighter since the den went quiet. The dead stay where we put them, mostly.

first_furrows.name: First Furrows

talk: Time you got your hands dirty. A rake, a seed dibber and a spade - any general store has them, the castle's included.
There are farming patches all along the roads between here, Ashvale and Saltmere. Find one, rake the weeds off and plant potato seeds.
Water them if you've a can, wait a few blocks, then dig me up three potatoes.
progress: Rake a patch, plant potato seeds, wait for them to grow, dig up three potatoes. The stores sell the seeds too.
complete: Three potatoes, and dirt to the elbows. You'll make a farmer yet. Here - onion seeds, for your next row.

talk: Onions next. They take a little longer and they make you cry when you cut them, which is how you know they're honest.
Plant those seeds I gave you and bring me news of three onions.
progress: Grow and dig up three onions. Farming level 5 to plant them.
complete: Three onions! The castle cook will have them before you can blink. You know your way round a patch now.

done: Tobin nods at every farming patch you pass, as if they were old friends of his.

lodge_greens.name: Greens for the Lodge

talk: The lodge's stew has been mostly water and optimism since the snows came. It needs greens.
Grow me four cabbages in one of the patches down by the roads. Farming 9 should do it.
progress: Four cabbages, grown in a farming patch by the roads below.
complete: Four fat cabbages. The stew will be a stew again. Sit down, have a bowl - you earned the first one.

done: The lodge's stew is famous now. Orla says it was always famous; it just hadn't been told.

moonleaf_for_the_circle.name: Moonleaf for the Circle

talk: Frost ink is half summit cold and half moonleaf, and the goblins have left us short of both.
Moonleaf will only grow in the large farming patches - rare things, by the roads below. Farming 33, and patience.
Two leaves. Bring word when you have dug them up.
progress: Grow two moonleaf in a large farming patch. The seeds come off strong beasts, now and then.
complete: Two moonleaf, silver as the beacon. The Circle's ink will be blacker than ever, which is to say paler, which is how frost ink works.

done: The Circle writes in moonleaf ink now. Halvard says you can taste the difference. Pell says not to.

sisters_barrow.name: The Sisters' Barrow

talk: So Isolde's den is quiet. Good. Then you can stand to hear the rest of it.
South of the moor, past the last of the fences, is the barrow where the Thornwatch buries its own. A week ago I sent Corva out to bury the sisters we lost on the road. Best eye in the camp.
She came back at dusk with a quiver full of black arrows and put two of them through the sentry on the bridge. She never said a word.
Now the barrow's dead are up out of their graves, and she walks among them like a shepherd with her flock. Whatever woke under the abbey has her.

Lay a dozen of the dead back down, so the barrow can hold its own again, and then put Corva down. Cleanly. She was my sister. Do it, and the Thornwatch will teach you to shoot like one of us. Cross the moor south; the iron gate stands open.
progress: {left} still walk in the barrow, {name}. A dozen of the dead, and Corva.
Corva is still out there, {name}. Close the distance; she will not let you stand off and trade arrows with her.
Strike her and every corpse near her comes running. Thin out the graves first, or fight with your back to the railing.
Elin has potions by the gate. You will want them.
complete: It's done, then. I thought I would feel something. Maybe later.
Here: a shortbow of the sisters' yew, and arrows to go with it. Hold it like this. No, lower. You'll learn.
The Thornwatch will remember who gave Corva her rest.

done: The barrow is quiet. Some nights I walk out and sit by her grave. The dead don't trouble me there any more.

caged_seer.name: The Caged Seer

talk: The barrow is quiet, and Rhosyn sleeps again. Thank you for that. Now I need you further south than any of us have dared.
There was a man named Hollin, the last of the old seers. He lived in Emberfall, a hamlet past the woods. When the abbey fell he sent us word, and then nothing.
Hollin would have known what woke under the abbey. If he is alive, we need him.
Emberfall cannot be reached by any road now. But the seers kept a way: five old stones in the field below the barrow, and a scroll that wakes them.
The scroll was hidden in the hollow oak, deep in the Gloamwood, past the stone field. Bring it to me. Whatever keeps the oak will not give it up kindly.
progress: The hollow oak stands at the far end of the Gloamwood, {name}, past the stone field and down the old path.
Reach into the hollow. Be ready when the tree answers.
Elin has potions by the gate. The wood eats the careless.
complete: Let me see it. Bark-paper, red thread. Hollin's own knot.
Five stones, five beasts cut in them, and the order to wake them: the Hawk first, then the Hound, then the Hart, then the Hare, and the Heron last.
Wake them in that order and they will open a way to Emberfall. Touch the wrong one and it will only stay cold.

talk: An ashling chief has taken the stones for his own. Rakkas, the scouts call him; he spits lightning. He will not let you near them while he lives.
Hawk, Hound, Hart, Hare, Heron. Then step through, find Hollin, and bring him home.
progress: Rakkas keeps the stones and Bregan keeps the cage, {name}. Both must fall before the old man walks free.
Hawk, Hound, Hart, Hare, Heron. The ring in the middle opens when the last one wakes.
complete: You're not one of them. You're real. Oh, thank the stars.
Bregan had the key. He was our smith; I watched him try to put the fire out with his hands. It got into him instead.
There. Help me down. My legs have forgotten what they are for.

talk: I know the way to your camp; the stones will take me. Go ahead and tell Isolde that Hollin is coming. Slowly, but coming.
And tell her the abbey's bells rang the night it fell. I heard them from here. Bells do not ring themselves.
progress: Hollin has gone ahead to the camp, {name}. Speak to Mother Isolde.
complete: Hollin is by the fire, eating as if he has not eaten in a month, which he hasn't. You brought him out of the fire.
Take this helm. It was made in the abbey's forge, before the abbey fell. It suits you better than it suited the wall it hung on.
He says he knows what woke under the abbey. He wants to speak to you himself.

done: Hollin talks to the fire more than to us. Go and sit with him, {name}. He has more to tell.

drowned_tower.name: The Drowned Tower

talk: Sit a moment. I have been reading the stones' old book while you were gone, and it tells of the Blackmere, past the Gloamwood.
There was a village in that bog once, and a tower over it. The lady of the tower was Morwen, a countess, and she was afraid of growing old.
The book says she bathed in what she took from the village girls, and the bog rose and drowned it all. Her and the tower with it.
She is down there still, at the bottom of the cellars, and whatever woke under the abbey has woken her too. She sits on a hoard the size of a hayrick.
Go through the Gloamwood past the oak and out its far side into the bog. The tower's stair goes down four levels. Bring her down, and the hoard is yours.
progress: Morwen is at the bottom of the tower, {name}. Four levels down.
Her maids come running when she calls. Fight them in a doorway if you can.
Take Mother Isolde's potions. The bog is no place to run short.
complete: You're back, and you smell of the bog. So it is done.
Keep the gold; she will not miss it. And take this from me, for what it is worth: you are the first in three hundred years to come up out of that tower.
There is more in the book. Gwen has been asking after you too; something about her hammer.

done: The Blackmere is only a bog again. Let it be.

smiths_hammer.name: The Smith's Hammer

talk: A word, before Gwen sees us talking. She will never ask you herself; she is too proud, and it is her own fault.
When we ran from the abbey she left her hammer on the anvil. Her master's hammer, and his master's. She has worked with borrowed tools ever since, and it shows.
The abbey is south of the Blackmere: follow the way out of the bog past the tower. Our old forgekeeper, Gorrath, kept the barracks forge. He turned with the rest.
Scouts say he is still at the anvil, hammering at nothing, day and night. With her hammer.
Bring it back to me and I will see it gets to her. And mind the sisters on the walls; they have not forgotten how to shoot.
progress: The barracks are against the abbey's west wall, {name}. Gorrath is at the forge.
Bring me Gwen's hammer. He will not give it up while he can stand.
The sisters keep their distance and shoot. Close in, or fight them round a corner.
complete: That's it. That's the hammer. Gwen! Gwen, come here.
...She will not say anything, but look at her face. She has been at the anvil since you walked in.
There. A longsword, out of the abbey's own steel, with her own hammer. And the stone to the abbey's portal stand in the yard: hold it and you can come and go.
One more thing is left, {name}. Mother Isolde wants you. It is about what lies under the abbey.

done: Gwen sings at the anvil now. Badly. Nobody minds.

thorn_maiden.name: The Thorn Maiden

talk: Hollin has told me what woke under the abbey, and I believe him, because I have felt it every night since we ran.
Her name is Maelis. The Maiden of Thorns. She was a sister of ours once, three hundred years ago, buried in the crypts with a thorn through her heart for what she did.
Someone pulled the thorn. Now her thorns are in our sisters, and they do what she wants.
The crypt stair is behind the altar in the cathedral. Four levels down she waits. Her thorns are poisoned; carry antidotes, and Elin's potions, as many as you can.
Put her back in the ground, {name}, and the Thornwatch can go home.
progress: Maelis is at the bottom of the crypts, {name}. Four levels under the cathedral.
Her thorns poison. Elin sells antidotes. Take them.
The stone Gwen's hammer bought you brings you to the abbey yard. Use it.
complete: I felt her go. All of us did. Rhosyn sat down in the mud and laughed until she cried.
Take this armour. It was the abbey's best, and it belongs to whoever brought the abbey back.
Tavish says the road east is open again; the thorns that closed it are dead. The Thornwatch goes home tomorrow. Some of us, anyway.
Thank you, {name}. The Sisters will remember your name for as long as there are Sisters.

done: The bells rang this morning. Nobody pulled the ropes. I think they were glad.

captains_cutlass.name: The Captain's Cutlass

talk: My lucky cutlass went over the side, or so Toby swears. Funny how a blade that sinks turns up for sale in a tavern.
Ask Tolly the dockhand. The tide brings everything to the third pier, the one with the bad plank.
say: The third pier? Nothing came ashore but weed and a boot, and the boot was mine.
Ask at the Tap. Things that don't wash up get drunk instead.
progress: Ask Tolly the dockhand on the piers whether the tide brought a cutlass in.
complete: Nothing washed up. As I thought. Somebody walked it ashore.

talk: Try Hollis at the Tap. If a blade was sold for drink in this town, Hollis poured the drink.
Be polite. He has a cudgel under the bar and a long memory.
say: A fancy cutlass? A man from the warehouses sold one for three rounds and a story. The story was better than the cutlass.
He went back to the North Warehouse. They all go back to the North Warehouse.
progress: Ask Hollis at the Saltmere Tap who sold a cutlass for drink.
complete: The North Warehouse. Smugglers. Of course it's smugglers. It's always smugglers in this harbour.

talk: Two of them loiter at the North Warehouse door, by the sound of it, minding a crate. My cutlass will be on one of them.
Explain to them, firmly, whose it is.
progress: Deal with the two smugglers at the North Warehouse door and get the cutlass off them.
complete: Two smugglers fewer. If the cutlass isn't in your hand yet, it's on the cobbles by that warehouse.

talk: Now bring it here. Every nick in that blade is a story, and most of the stories are lies, but they're my lies.
The smugglers drop it as often as they hold it. Look about you.
progress: Bring Captain Ruark his cutlass. The smugglers at the North Warehouse have it.
complete: That's her. And I know Toby sold it; there's only one fool aboard who'd trade steel for a story.
I'm not angry. I'm impressed. Here - a cutlass of your own, and coin for your trouble. Don't sell it for drink.

done: Ruark tells the cutlass story differently every time. In the newest one, you are a sea serpent.

fish_stew_again.name: Fish Stew Again

talk: Forty days of fish stew. The crew are starting to look like fish. Soot has grown fins, I swear it.
First, salt. Nettie the fishmonger keeps a sea salt better than mine. She'll want fish for it, mind - two raw shrimp.
progress: Take two raw shrimp to Nettie the fishmonger for a twist of sea salt.
complete: Two shrimp for a twist of salt - fair trade. Tell Grizz it's for stew, not for preserving the crew.

talk: Now the part that grew in the ground. Three potatoes, three onions - farm them, buy them, I won't ask.
Put them in a pot at any fire with the salt and a cooked shrimp, and bring me a pirate's stew. A stew. With things in it.
progress: At any fire, cook 3 potatoes, 3 onions, the sea salt and a cooked shrimp into a pirate's stew, and bring it to Grizz.
complete: Potatoes! Onions! Something that isn't fish! The crew will weep.
Soot says he saw a carrot in the sky this morning. I've stopped arguing with Soot.

done: Grizz makes the stew every Friday now. On the other days it's still fish.

black_sails.name: Black Sails

talk: The mainsail's torn and the captain won't sail with a patched sail. Canvas costs money. Money costs questions.
Get me canvas, no questions. Sela the chandler has canvas. Start there.
say: Canvas I have. Twine strong enough to hold a mainsail in a gale I haven't - that's tarred rope, and Bryce knows how to use it.
I'll sell you both. I won't ask what it's for, and you won't tell me it's for nets.
progress: Ask Sela the chandler about sail canvas.
complete: Sela has it. Good. She never asks questions she can't sell the answers to.

talk: Buy a bolt of canvas and three coils of tarred rope from Sela, and take them to Bryce the shipwright.
He'll stitch it into a mainsail and row it out himself. He likes us. He thinks we're a fishing boat.
progress: Take a bolt of sail canvas and three tarred ropes to Bryce the shipwright.
complete: A mainsail? For a fishing boat? With a skull on it? ...I'll have it stitched by the tide and rowed out to her. Don't tell me any more.

talk: Trouble. Mayor Calder has heard there's a pirate ship in his harbour.
Talk him out of it. You have the face for it. It's a fishing boat, Mayor, with ambitious sails. It needs a good tongue: Speechcraft 15 at least.
progress: Talk Mayor Calder out of the notion that there's a pirate ship in his harbour (Speechcraft 15).
complete: A fishing boat. With ambitious sails. ...Very well. But if it fishes for anything that isn't fish, I'll hear of it.

talk: Come back and tell me it's done. I'll write it down as 'nets'.
Everything gets written down as nets.
progress: Tell Quartermaster Grix the sail is stitched and the Mayor is quiet.
complete: Sail stitched, Mayor quiet, and not one question. 'Nets.' There.
The captain sends you his spare tricorn. He has six. He says a hat makes the sailor.

done: Grix's ledger lists four hundred nets. The ship has never carried a net.

the_admiral.name: The Admiral

talk: There's a cat that sleeps in the rum store. I call her Admiral. She's gone off, and the quartermaster says that's one less mouth.
She'll be in the alleys behind the quay. Find her and give her a scratch - she comes back for a scratch.
progress: Find Admiral, a black and white cat, in Saltmere's alleys, and pet her.
complete: She purrs like a ship's bilge pump and follows you a step or two. Toby will want to know.

talk: You found her? Go on, tell me where. No - don't, she'd hate that.
Just tell me she's all right.
progress: Tell Toby the cabin boy that Admiral is safe.
complete: She'll come back to the rum barrels now she knows someone looked. Thanks. When I get my sword, you can hold it first.

done: Admiral sleeps on the rum barrels again. Grix has stopped counting her as a mouth.

tutorial_island.name: Tutorial Island

talk: Welcome to the valley!
Guide Elsbeth is right beside you.
steps.hint: Click Guide Elsbeth, under the gold arrow, to say hello.
progress: Click Guide Elsbeth, under the gold arrow, to say hello.
complete: Hello, and welcome! We're so glad you've come. I'm Elsbeth, and I'll help you find your feet.
To walk, click on the ground. To talk to someone, click on them - just like you did with me! The box at the top always says what to do next.

talk: Your first stop is Survivalist Marlow, by the trees to the west.
Follow the gold arrow above his head. Off you go!
steps.hint: Follow the gold arrow to Survivalist Marlow and click him.
progress: Follow the gold arrow to Survivalist Marlow and click him.
complete: Hello there! Elsbeth said a new friend was coming. Welcome - you're going to love it here.

talk: Let's start with a campfire. I've put a hatchet and a tinderbox in your pack - the bag button on the right shows your pack.
Click a tree to chop some logs. Then click the logs in your pack and choose Light.
steps.hint: Click a tree to chop logs. Then click the logs in your pack and choose Light.
progress: Click a tree to chop logs. Then click the logs in your pack and choose Light.
complete: Look at that - your very first fire! Well done. Every adventurer remembers their first fire.

talk: Now let's catch some dinner. Here's a fishing net.
Click the bubbling water on the shore to catch a shrimp, then click your fire to cook it.
steps.hint: Click the bubbling water to catch a shrimp. Then click your fire to cook it.
progress: Click the bubbling water to catch a shrimp. Then click your fire to cook it.
complete: Perfectly cooked! You're a natural.

talk: Gardener Fen's garden is just to the north. I've put a rake, a seed dibber, a spade and two radish seeds in your pack.
Click the farming patch there: Rake it, Plant a seed, wait a moment, then Harvest.
steps.hint: Click the farming patch: Rake, then Plant a radish seed, wait, then Harvest. Grow 2 radishes.
progress: Click the farming patch: Rake, then Plant a radish seed, wait, then Harvest. Grow 2 radishes.
complete: Two radishes, grown by you! Brilliant. There are farming patches all along the valley's roads, and every one can be yours.

talk: Next, Loremaster Ilse, by the big stone. She looks after the quest journal.
Click the Quests button on the right - the one that looks like a scroll - to open it, then go and see her.
steps.hint: Click the Quests button on the right (the scroll), then talk to Loremaster Ilse.
progress: Click the Quests button on the right (the scroll), then talk to Loremaster Ilse.
complete: That's your quest journal! A quest is a story told in steps. The journal always shows the step you're on, so you never get lost.
Every quest you finish earns story points. You're already on your first one - this island!

talk: Prospector Dunn is digging by the rocks to the south. Take him this pickaxe.
Click a copper rock to mine some ore, then bring it to Dunn.
steps.hint: Click a copper rock to mine one copper ore. Then talk to Prospector Dunn.
progress: Click a copper rock to mine one copper ore. Then talk to Prospector Dunn.
complete: Lovely bit of copper! Ore is how you'll make things one day. You're a miner now, too.

talk: Sergeant Kade is waiting to the east, by the rats. He sent you this sword.
Click the sword in your pack and choose Wield. The Equipment button - the shirt - shows what you're holding and wearing.
steps.hint: Click the sword in your pack and choose Wield. Then talk to Sergeant Kade.
progress: Click the sword in your pack and choose Wield. Then talk to Sergeant Kade.
complete: There - armed and ready! Now let's put that sword to work.

talk: See those island rats? Click one to fight it. Your sword does the rest.
Defeat two, then come back to me.
steps.hint: Click an island rat to fight it. Defeat 2 rats, then talk to Sergeant Kade.
progress: Click an island rat to fight it. Defeat 2 rats, then talk to Sergeant Kade.
complete: Ha! Two rats, and barely a scratch on you. You fight like a hero already!

talk: Fighting is hungry work. Your health is the red circle at the top right.
Click the bread in your pack and choose Eat - food heals you whenever you're hurt.
steps.hint: Click the bread in your pack and choose Eat. Then talk to Sergeant Kade.
progress: Click the bread in your pack and choose Eat. Then talk to Sergeant Kade.
complete: Good! Always eat before your health gets low. That's the best advice I've got.

talk: Now, from a distance. Here's a bow and some arrows.
Wield the bow, then click a rat to shoot it.
steps.hint: Click the bow in your pack and choose Wield. Then click a rat to shoot it.
progress: Click the bow in your pack and choose Wield. Then click a rat to shoot it.
complete: A fine shot! Bows let you fight from far away.

talk: And last, magic. Here's a staff - no spellbook needed.
Wield the staff and click a rat to cast a spell at it.
steps.hint: Click the staff in your pack and choose Wield. Then click a rat to cast a spell.
progress: Click the staff in your pack and choose Wield. Then click a rat to cast a spell.
complete: Magic! You've tried every way to fight - sword, bow and staff. Keep whichever you like best. I'm proud of you.

talk: Banker Corin keeps the chest by the jetty. He'll show you how to keep your things safe.
Click the chest, then click something in your pack to put it in.
steps.hint: Click the bank chest, then click an item in your pack to put it in. Then talk to Banker Corin.
progress: Click the bank chest, then click an item in your pack to put it in. Then talk to Banker Corin.
complete: Safely stored! The chest keeps your things even when your pack is full.

talk: Now take it back out. Click the chest, then click the item in the chest.
Don't worry - nothing gets lost in there.
steps.hint: Click the bank chest and click the item to take it back out. Then talk to Banker Corin.
progress: Click the bank chest and click the item to take it back out. Then talk to Banker Corin.
complete: Back in your pack! There's a chest like this in every town in the valley, and they're all yours.

talk: Ledger-keeper Asha is beside the chest. She'll explain your wallet.
Click the bank chest once more - your wallet is shown there: your address and what you own.
steps.hint: Click the bank chest to see your wallet. Then talk to Ledger-keeper Asha.
progress: Click the bank chest to see your wallet. Then talk to Ledger-keeper Asha.
complete: That's your wallet: your address, and the things that are truly yours. 'Kept on chain' means they're recorded on the blockchain - they belong to you, not to the game.
Please back up your wallet: write down your recovery words, keep them somewhere safe, and never share them with anyone - not even me.
One more thing: right now the valley runs on a test network, so coins and items have no real money value yet. Enjoy learning!

talk: Trader Milo runs the stall by the path. Let's do some shopping.
Click Milo and choose Trade, then click something on his shelf to buy it.
steps.hint: Click Trader Milo, choose Trade, and click something on his shelf to buy it.
progress: Click Trader Milo, choose Trade, and click something on his shelf to buy it.
complete: A fine purchase! Shops all over the valley work just the same.

talk: Now sell me something back - anything you don't need. Click it in your pack while my shop is open.
Even a radish is worth a coin or two to me!
steps.hint: Open Trader Milo's shop again and click something in your pack to sell it.
progress: Open Trader Milo's shop again and click something in your pack to sell it.
complete: Pleasure doing business! Selling what you don't need is how you'll earn coins.

talk: Brother Aldo keeps the little chapel to the north-east. Take these bones to him.
Click the bones in your pack and choose Bury - it trains your Prayer.
steps.hint: Click the bones in your pack and choose Bury. Then talk to Brother Aldo.
progress: Click the bones in your pack and choose Bury. Then talk to Brother Aldo.
complete: Well done. Burying bones trains your Prayer, and prayers protect you in a fight.

talk: Open the Prayer button on the right, and click a prayer to switch it on.
Any one will do - they all help keep you safe in a fight.
steps.hint: Click the Prayer button on the right and click a prayer to switch it on. Then talk to Brother Aldo.
progress: Click the Prayer button on the right and click a prayer to switch it on. Then talk to Brother Aldo.
complete: There - you're protected. Prayers use prayer points; recharge them at any altar. Go in peace, friend.

talk: You've learned everything you need! Ferryman Odo is waiting at the pier in the south-east.
Follow the arrow - your adventure in Ashvale is about to begin!
steps.hint: Follow the arrow to Ferryman Odo at the pier and click him.
progress: Follow the arrow to Ferryman Odo at the pier and click him.
complete: You did it - you've finished Tutorial Island! Everyone here is proud of you.
Hop in. In Ashvale, talk to Elder Maren by the well - she has your first real quest. Welcome to the valley!
